full_judgment:
3. Plaintiff's case, in short, is that the suit holding belonged to Sheikh Piru who was the owner the land of C.S. Khatian No. 639 bearing the suit plot and other plots and he died leaving 3 sons, namely, Cherag Ali Sheikh, Nowab Ali and Sheikh Wahed Ali and their names were correctly recorded in the C.S. Khatian No. 639 (Exb.1); Said 3 brothers were in possession of the suit holding by amicable arrangement plots wise and area wise which also has been depicted in the C.S. Khatian and accordingly Cherage Ali was possessing and owing the suit plot which has been shown in the C.S. Khatian (Ext.1) After death of Cherag Ali has heirs sold 30 decimals land of the suit plot to Rajkumar Bhattacherjee and his there other brothers by registered kabala on 03.02.1941 vide Exb.2; Later on said Rajkumar Bhattacherjee and his three other brothers settled the said 30 decimals of land for agricultural purpose to Ahmed Bapari in Poush 1357 B.S and delivered possession of the same to him Ahmed Bepari since was in possession from Poush 1357 B.S. his name was recorded in the R.S. Khatian (Exb-3); said Ahmed Bepari since was in possession as owner of the said land sold out the same to the plaintiff on 26.06.1965 vide Exb. 4. In that sale deed, Jonah Ali, son of Nowab Ali, a full brother of the defendant Nos. 1-3, Haider Ali son of the Janab Ali Lal Miah son of Ahmed Bepari Were witnesses and the seller delivered possession the purchaser plaintiff; Jonab Ali father of the defendant No. 8 Haider Ali executed a Barga Kabuliat (exbt.5) in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit land for 5 years in the year 1968 as the bargader of the suit land under the plaintiff. 

 6. Defendant Nos.1-7 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement and later on an additional written statement was also filed by the defendants, contending, inter alia, that the suit holding , was never partitioned among Cherag Ali and his other co-sharers and Cherag Ali never enjoyed the suit plot alone and his heir’s sale of said 30 decimal land to Rajkumar Bhattacharjee and others was not correct and Rajkumar Bhattacharjee and his brothers did not enjoy the suit land and their subsequent settlement in favour of Ahmed Bepari was false and sale by Ahmed Bepari to the plaintiff is not legal and genuine and the some of the plaintiff is not legal and genuine and the name of the plaintiff was wrongly recorded in the S.A. Khatian and that-defendants as heirs of Nowab Ali, a brother of Cherag Ali are possessing the suit plot. The plaintiff has no right, title or possession in the suit land. 

 15. D.W.1 Yunus Ali Admitted in cross examination that in C.S. khatian against the disputed Plot No. 219 possession of Cherag Ali has been written. He did not deny the sale of the suit land by the heirs of Charag Ali to Rajumar Bhattacharjee and others. In cross-examination he said he does not know if three sons and one daughter of Cherag Ali sold the suit land in 1941 to Rajkumar Bhattacharjee and others. He also has not denied Rajkumar Bhattacharjee and his brothers transferred .30 acres land in favour of the Ahmed Bepari. He has also stated, “আহম্মদ ব্যাপারী দখল করা কালে বাদীর নিকট ১৯৬৫ সালে বিক্রয় করে দেয় কিনা জানি না।” In a civil litigaiton onus of prove does not remain constant as in criminal litigation. D.W.3 Md. Hyber Ali son of Jonab Ali did not deny existence of Exts. 5 and 5(2). D.W. 6 Abdul Jalil has stated in cross-examination ''নালিশী সম্পত্তি আগে মালিক ছিল নবাব চেরাগ, ওয়াহেদ আলী। আহম্মদ ব্যাপারী নাঃ দাগের কোন অংশ দথল করত বলতে পারি না।
